Resolves #2392

Local Stores can now keep an edited record in sorted order by enabling `reapplyOnRecordChange` on a sorter. Existing sorters retain their current edit behavior. The Store uses its existing complete sort before publishing the record's new index, including calculated/dotted fields and opaque comparator dependencies; remote and paged projections keep their existing policy.

Evidence: L2 (real Model/Store contract tests in the single-thread engine harness) → L2 required for this data-policy change. No installed-runtime or visual acceptance claim.

## AC Evidence

No structured ACs on #2392. The [intake contract](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/issues/2392#issuecomment-6655580648) is covered by `test/playwright/unit/data/StoreRecordSort.spec.mjs`: opt-in/default behavior, eager/lazy records, filtered membership, multi-sort and batched edits, virtual/calculated/dotted fields, lifetime guards, settled key maps, and hierarchical TreeStore sorting.

## Deltas from ticket

Automatic edit sorting is opt-in per sorter, matching the existing Filter option and preserving edit stability by default. `autoSort: false` still opts out. Custom comparators and virtual sort fields conservatively reapply on every record edit. A filter pass that already sorts is reused. TreeStore key-map updates now run inside the existing Store notification transaction through `updateKeyMaps`, so sorting cannot observe half-updated structural maps. This adds the requested capability; no existing consumer workaround was removed.

## Test Evidence

All coverage runs in CI. The new ordering cases failed before the implementation; existing filtering/default-policy controls passed. Local surrounding Store/TreeStore/Collection suites passed. `agent-preflight` is not hosted in this Engine checkout; PR-body, class-module-scope, diff and file-size checks were run directly.

## Post-Merge Validation

None required beyond the source and contract tests; this does not change any application's sorter opt-in.

Thanks, Grace. The exact-head approval and contract audit are consumed; live GitHub now shows the human merge.

One refinement to the cost hypothesis: the no-`fields` call in `updateKey` decides whether to open the notification transaction. When a reactive Record emits a change, the later `onRecordChange(change)` checks its **actual changed fields** before sorting. The unconditional conservative fallback is the raw-item/no-notification path; custom and virtual sorts also intentionally have wider read sets. A bulk-sync measurement should distinguish those cases before turning this into a defect. No additional work item is warranted from an unmeasured cost hypothesis alone.

The protected-hook suggestion is a non-blocking extension point consideration, with no remaining required action or accepted follow-up dependency on this delivery.

*   **Inputs Read Before Patch:** #2392 (the operator, 2021: an edit to a sorted field "should trigger collection.doSort()"), `Store.onRecordChange` / `updateKey` on `dev`, the `Filter.reapplyOnRecordChange` precedent and its grid-menu consumer, the intake contract (issuecomment-6655580648), and today's operator ruling that an `op` ticket closes once the still-valid parts of its intent survive.
*   **Expected Solution Shape:** The record-change policy lives in `Store`. The rule lives on `Sorter`, opt-in like Filter's. Sorting happens before `recordChange` publishes its index and runs through the existing `doSort` paths (flat and tree). Remote and paged projections are excluded. A recursion guard covers tree statistics. It must not change behavior for any existing sorter, and specs must own and destroy their Stores.
*   **Patch Verdict:** Matches. `shouldReapplySorters` gates on `autoSort`, loading and streaming, and `isPipelinePushProjectionUncertain()` (`remoteFilter || remoteSort || pageSize > 0`). It sorts only a record that is still current (`map`/`get(key) === record`), and treats callbacks and virtual fields conservatively. `#sortingRecordChange` is set inside a `try`/`finally`.
*   **Premise Coherence:** Coheres with verify-before-assert. The 2021 intent was re-checked against current source before it shipped, and the still-valid part (edits re-sort) ships as a capability, not as a default that changes every consumer.

### 🔬 Depth Floor

**Challenge OR documented search (per guide §7.1):**

- **Challenge** (`hypothesis — needs V-B-A before implementation`): Inside `updateKey`, `shouldReapplySorters({record: item})` has no `fields`, so any opted-in sorter counts as affected and every key change runs a full `doSort`. With bulk key changes on an opted-in store (for example, server ids replacing phantom ids after a create sync), that becomes one O(n log n) sort per record, with no batch to coalesce them. It is opt-in and needs a measurement before it is a defect, so it is not an action here. A second, smaller point: `onRecordChange` now asks `hasNtype('tree-store')` in the base class, beside the existing `updateKey` check. A protected "does my filter pass sort?" hook would let TreeStore answer for itself.
